limits: Logged clones retain actual columns, defaults and indexes, but have no foreign keys or product triggers. UUID-only synthetic rows; not canonical ingest throughput.

notes: Filesystem caches were not dropped; this is a reused corpus on a shared host, not a cold-disk sustained-dump measurement.
Final pre-spawn cancellation cleanup was tested separately; the successful measured path is unchanged.
Source/decompressed MiB rates divide the verified input byte totals by canonical wall-clock; they are not isolated ZIP/decompression capacity measurements.

One final timed run per profile on a shared host without CPU/RAM quotas. A and B source concurrency 4; C uses 2 with identical total parser/commit budgets. Small canonical gain is not a statistical guarantee.

Canonical timing starts at persisted batch started_at and ends at the last successful ingestRecords return; batch-final cleanup/state time is separate. End-to-end includes queue drain, refresh and all-ID/generation plus authenticated sample reader checks.

The exact current/historical/full-text queue counts at the last commit are approximated by the first following ~1 s sample. OpenSearch node doc count can include Lucene deleted/nested documents; it is not the canonical searchable-work count. Final all-ID verification is authoritative.

CPU seconds and inclusive SQL/COPY/checkpoint/staging/pack spans overlap and must not be summed into wall-clock. API shares the worker benchmark container. Per-process CPU is sampled; a process can exit between samples.

Named staging sampling excludes anonymous/unlinked spool files. B/C reservations include these files and conservatively retained credits/input buffers, but exclude PackStore temporary packs (included in named staging). Baseline additional anonymous-spool upper bound is the sum of largest members above 8 MiB per source: 386955863 bytes, not a measured simultaneous peak.

Physical filesystem totals include cluster/WAL and OpenSearch translog and were captured after the timed drain/integrity verification, before queue-shape probes or replay. SQL database/index sizes and primary index bytes are separate. Filesystem cache contents and residual staging are zero.

The first B attempt stopped safely at 2071 committed works because an initial per-record staging estimate rejected a 262421940-byte member. Excluded from timing comparisons; replaced by shared per-source byte reservations, preserving the 4 GiB global budget.

B/C are measured from the final implementation, including global slots for single records, tags and auxiliary ZIP artifacts. Earlier B/C coordination probes are excluded from the main comparison. A uses the original P3A implementation.

Queue storage probe uses logged table clones with production columns/indexes, 100000 synthetic UUIDs, no foreign keys/triggers. It is a queue-operation measurement, not canonical ingest. One-million estimates are linear extrapolations. DELETE/VACUUM retain index pages; physical byte policy accounts for that.

Normalized comparisons retain content, metadata, versions and provenance; only validated local UUID references and non-semantic search generation/epoch/ingestion-time fields are normalized as in P3A. Tag keyword arrays are sorted, preserving multiplicity. Raw content hashes are also checked.
